findings.title: 8 of 37 CLI subcommands have zero test coverage (gen, repl, expand, jupyter, bench_compile, bench_program, extract_function, inline_variable)
findings.description: The CLI defines 37+ subcommand variants in cli.rs (Build/Run/New/Gen/.../Rename/ExtractFunction/InlineVariable). A case-insensitive name-mention scan (CamelCase + snake_case + squashed forms) of all 40 files in crates/buff-lang-cli/tests found zero references to Gen, Repl, Expand, Jupyter, BenchCompile, BenchProgram, ExtractFunction, and InlineVariable. The buff-jupyter and buff-repl crates have their own unit tests, but the CLI dispatch layer for `buff jupyter install`, `buff repl`, `buff gen`, `buff expand`, and the extract/inline refactor operations is never driven by any test. refactor_tests.rs covers only the `rename` operation.
findings.root_cause: Subcommands were added across v1.13-v1.20 waves without a per-subcommand test-acceptance criterion; the CI test jobs are advisory (continue-on-error) so the gap never surfaced as a gate failure.
findings.impact: Regressions in argument parsing, flag handling, or dispatch for ~22% of the user-facing command surface (including two of three `buff refactor` operations and the Jupyter install path) can ship undetected; breakage is only discovered by end users.
findings.recommendation: Add one integration test file per untested subcommand in crates/buff-lang-cli/tests/ driving the lib API (`buff_lang_cli::commands::*`) without subprocess, per the crate's own AGENTS.md convention. Start with jupyter (install into temp dir), gen, and the two refactor ops (extract_function, inline_variable).

fix_examples.before:
// no test exists for `buff gen` anywhere in crates/buff-lang-cli/tests/
// (grep 'gen' across all 40 test files returns 0 matches)

findings.fix_guide: 1) Read crates/buff-lang-cli/src/cli.rs to get each variant's args struct. 2) Locate the matching commands/<name>.rs entry fn (all 8 have one). 3) Write a tests/<name>_command.rs file driving the lib fn directly with tempdir inputs, asserting on produced files/stdout payload, not just Ok. 4) Run `cargo test -p buff-lang-cli --test <name>_command`.

effort_estimate.human_readable: ~1 day (8 tests x ~30-60 min incl. reading each commands/<name>.rs signature)
effort_estimate.breakdown: API discovery: 120; test authoring: 240; debugging assertions: 80; verification run: 40

detection_method.query: for each Command enum variant V in cli.rs: regex '(?i)\\bV\\b|\\bsnake(V)\\b' against concatenation of crates/buff-lang-cli/tests/*.rs -> 0 matches for 8 variants

confidence.rationale: Name-mention scan is a heuristic: a test could exercise a subcommand via a constant or helper without naming it. Mitigated by checking CamelCase, snake_case, and squashed forms across all 40 test files; all 8 returned exactly 0.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Zero mentions of any spelling form across the full test corpus; per-subcommand modules in commands/ make indirect unnamed testing unlikely. Verified the inverse direction too: BenchColdStart correctly shows up via bench_cold_start.rs, so the heuristic does produce positives.

findings.title: Golden fixture gate exercises only 5 of 62 stable ErrorCodes; E14xx runtime family has zero fixtures
findings.description: code.rs defines 62 stable ErrorCode variants (E1001-E1014 lex, E1101-E1110 parse, E1201-E1214 type, E1301-E1304 codegen, E1401-E1410 runtime, E1501-E1510 lint) that are promised stable forever. The dedicated fixture-coverage gate (error_code_coverage.rs, 178 lines) asserts exactly 5 codes: E1001, E1102, E1202, E1301, E1501. tests/fixtures/invalid/ holds 11 .buff fixtures for a 62-code surface. A workspace-wide scan of all crates/*/tests/*.rs found only 13 distinct ErrorCode variants asserted anywhere in integration tests; the entire E14xx runtime family (GpuDispatchFailed, ShaderCompileFailed, ChannelClosed, etc. - 10 codes) and 9 of 14 lex codes (E1004-E1014) have no fixture and no integration assertion. The file's own doc table lists 6 fixtures where one exists only as documentation.
findings.root_cause: The fixture corpus was seeded once per phase (T51) with one representative error per phase category and never expanded as new ErrorCodes were added in v1.13-v1.39 (comptime, trait objects, multispan, GPU, channels).
findings.impact: ErrorCodes are a public stability contract ('stable forever'); any refactor of a diagnostic emission path for the 49 unexercised codes can silently change, misnumber, or drop the diagnostic with no failing test - directly violating the documented guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Expand tests/fixtures/invalid/ toward one fixture per stable ErrorCode (prioritize E1004-E1014 and E1103-E1110, which are cheap compile-time cases), and extend error_code_coverage.rs with a data-driven test table mapping fixture -> expected ErrorCode so every new code requires a fixture at review time.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Enumerate variants in crates/buff-lang-error/src/code.rs. 2) For each family, craft a minimal .buff trigger (lexer/parser/type codes are one-liners). 3) Add fixture + one assertion fn mirroring the existing pattern in error_code_coverage.rs. 4) E14xx needs buff-lang-runtime tests with the mock GPU backend instead of fixtures (documented as runtime-only). 5) Gate: `cargo test -p buff-lang-cli --test error_code_coverage`.

effort_estimate.human_readable: ~1.5 days for the 20 highest-value codes (lex/parse/type families); E14xx deferred to runtime crate
effort_estimate.breakdown: Trigger crafting: 300; fixture+assert pairs: 200; runtime-family spike: 60; verification: 40

detection_method.query: 62 variants extracted from 'pub enum ErrorCode' in code.rs vs 13 unique 'ErrorCode::X' matches across crates/*/tests/*.rs and 5 asserted in error_code_coverage.rs

findings.verification_command: $enum=[regex]::Match((Get-Content crates/buff-lang-error/src/code.rs -Raw),'pub enum ErrorCode\s*\{(.*?)\n\}','Singleline').Groups[1].Value; ($enum -split "`n" | Select-String '^\s{4}[A-Z]').Count; (Get-ChildItem crates -Recurse -Filter *.rs | Where-Object FullName -match '\\tests\\' | Select-String 'ErrorCode::([A-Za-z]+)' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object {$_.Matches}|ForEach-Object{$_.Groups[1].Value} | Sort-Object -Unique).Count

confidence.rationale: Both sides of the ratio are mechanically extracted (62 enum variants; 5 asserted codes in the fixture gate; 13 unique in integration tests). Caveat honored in text: inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests in src may cover additional codes, but they are indistinguishable from production construction sites by grep and are not golden-gated.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Fixture-gate coverage of exactly 5 codes is directly readable from the 178-line test file. The 13/62 integration figure counts only crates/*/tests/ files, stated explicitly; claim is scoped to fixtures + integration tests, not all possible test forms.

findings.title: Jupyter kernel protocol core (kernel.rs run loop + execution.rs) never driven by any test
findings.description: kernel.rs is the largest file in buff-jupyter (1,470 lines, 64KB) and exposes the entire kernel as `Kernel::new(transport, conn)` + `pub async fn run()` - the Jupyter message loop handling execute_request/execute_reply/iopub. The crate's 5 test files (connection_tests, hmac_tests, kernelspec_tests, kernel_info_tests, wire_tests; ~17KB total vs 175KB of src) import only the peripheral helpers: connection::ConnectionFile, hmac::{sign,verify}, kernelspec, messages::{KernelInfoReply, BANNER}, wire::{MessageHeader, WireMessage}. No test imports kernel::Kernel, calls run(), or performs an execute_request -> execute_reply/status=iopub round-trip. execution.rs (10.5KB, cross-cell state) is likewise unreferenced. kernel.rs contains no inline #[cfg(test)] module either.
findings.root_cause: T129 testing focused on the wire-protocol building blocks (HMAC signing, header serialization, connection-file parsing) because they are pure and trivially testable; the stateful kernel loop needs a mock transport + in-memory ZMQ substitute that was deferred and never revisited.
findings.impact: The single most user-visible behavior of the Jupyter integration - 'run this cell, get output, keep session state' - has zero regression protection. A protocol bug (wrong reply status, dropped iopub stream message, broken cross-cell state) would ship undetected and only appear as a broken kernel in real notebooks.
findings.recommendation: Add crates/buff-jupyter/tests/kernel_roundtrip.rs with a mock Transport impl (the Kernel is generic over T) feeding a scripted sequence: kernel_info_request, execute_request x2 (second referencing the first's binding), shutdown_request; assert reply msg_type/status/iopub ordering and cross-cell state survival. This requires no ZMQ - the generic transport boundary already exists.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Confirm the generic bound on Kernel::new (transport trait) in kernel.rs. 2) Implement a MockTransport over Vec<Vec<u8>> frames. 3) Script kernel_info + execute x2 + shutdown; drive the loop for N messages instead of forever (may need a small run-for-N test seam). 4) Assert msg_type sequence, reply status, iopub stream frames, and cross-cell state. 5) `cargo test -p buff-jupyter --test kernel_roundtrip`.

effort_estimate.human_readable: ~1 day (mock transport + loop seam + assertions; largest single item in this audit)
effort_estimate.breakdown: Transport trait study: 60; mock impl: 120; run-seam refactor if needed: 120; assertions: 80; verification: 40

detection_method.query: imports of buff_jupyter::* across crates/buff-jupyter/tests/*.rs vs 'pub fn' surface of src/kernel.rs (new/session_id/run); grep 'kernel|execution' in tests -> only kernelspec/kernel_info constants

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path crates/buff-jupyter/tests/*.rs -Pattern 'kernel::|Kernel::|execution|execute_request' | Measure-Object | Select-Object -Expand Count; Select-String -Path crates/buff-jupyter/src/kernel.rs -Pattern 'pub (async )?fn' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Line

confidence.rationale: File-by-file import scan of all 5 test files plus an inline-cfg(test) scan of kernel.rs; both empty for the kernel/execution modules. Only residual risk is an indirect test seam inside transport.rs consumed by kernel - but no test instantiates Kernel at all, so the loop remains unexercised regardless.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: No test file imports Kernel or execution; kernel.rs has no inline test module (verified via #[cfg(test)] scan of src root and subdirectories); public API is only new/session_id/run, so nothing else could indirectly exercise the loop.

findings.title: LSP server main loop (JSON-RPC handshake, dispatch, debounced diagnostics) has zero tests
findings.description: buff-lsp has a single integration test file (tests/capabilities.rs, 442 lines) which drives the pure handlers:: functions directly on DocumentState - good coverage of hover/completion/goto-def/symbols/formatting/diagnostics. However, no test references Connection, initialize, or server::run_stdio (grep across tests returns zero matches). The server.rs main loop - capability registration, request dispatch arms, didChange full-reparse plumbing, and the 300ms debounced diagnostics select loop - is completely untested, and server.rs carries no inline #[cfg(test)] module.
findings.root_cause: The T117 architecture deliberately isolated I/O in server.rs so handlers stay pure and testable; the loop itself was left to manual VSCode-extension verification (T118) and never backfilled with an in-process Connection test.
findings.impact: Dispatch regressions (unregistered capability, wrong method name, changed sync kind, broken debounce) compile fine and pass all handler tests but break the editor experience for every user of the bundled VSCode extension.
findings.recommendation: Add an in-process integration test using lsp_server::Connection::memory() (or a pair of crossbeam channels) to perform the initialize/initialized handshake against server::run loop entry, send textDocument/didOpen + didChange, and assert a publishDiagnostics notification arrives; then a shutdown/exit pair.

fix_examples.before:
// crates/buff-lsp/tests/*: zero matches for 'Connection|initialize|server::'
// handlers are tested directly: handlers::diagnostics(&open(src))

findings.fix_guide: 1) Check lsp-server 0.10 for Connection::memory() availability (else construct over crossbeam channels). 2) Factor a test entry in server.rs that takes a Connection instead of opening stdio. 3) Script initialize -> initialized -> didOpen(bad type) -> expect publishDiagnostics -> shutdown/exit. 4) `cargo test -p buff-lsp --test protocol`.

effort_estimate.breakdown: lsp-server API study: 60; entry refactor: 60; harness+assertions: 80; verification: 40

detection_method.query: grep 'Connection|initialize|server::' crates/buff-lsp/tests/*.rs -> 0 matches; handlers-only coverage confirmed by reading capabilities.rs header comment

findings.verification_command: (Select-String -Path crates/buff-lsp/tests/*.rs -Pattern 'Connection|initialize_request|server::' | Measure-Object).Count; Get-ChildItem crates/buff-lsp/tests -Filter *.rs | Measure-Object | Select-Object -Expand Count

confidence.rationale: Single test file in the crate, fully scanned imports; server loop provably not driven. Confidence held at 0.85 because an inline cfg(test) in server.rs covering loop helpers was not individually opened - though even if present it could not cover the transport loop which requires a Connection.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Crate has exactly one tests/ file (verified by directory listing) and the grep for loop-related symbols returns zero. The finding is scoped to the loop, not the handlers, which are explicitly acknowledged as well covered.

findings.title: All cargo test jobs are advisory (continue-on-error: true), so no test gap or regression can block a merge
findings.description: Both cargo test jobs in ci.yml (test-core at line 117, test-framework at line 145, the latter commented 'pre-existing API drift') run with continue-on-error: true, and CONTRIBUTING.md documents them under 'Advisory jobs (do not block merge)'. The repo's own README exit criteria ('cargo test --workspace -> 100% pass') are therefore enforced nowhere. This converts every other finding in this audit from 'already partially mitigated by CI' to 'fully unprotected': a red test suite passes silently.
findings.root_cause: Tests were made advisory to keep merges flowing while framework-crate API drift (acknowledged in the ci.yml comment) was worked down; the promotion back to gate was never scheduled.
findings.impact: Regression protection exists on paper only. Combined with the coverage gaps above, silent breakage can ship in any merge; contributors have no signal that tests fail unless they run them locally via scripts/local-ci.ps1.
findings.recommendation: Time-box a drift-elimination sprint to make the failing subset green, then flip test-framework to continue-on-error: false, followed by test-core on ubuntu. Keep the 3-OS matrix advisory one extra cycle if platform flakiness is the concern.

fix_examples.before:
test-framework:
    continue-on-error: true   # line 145, 'pre-existing API drift'
fix_examples.after:
test-framework:
    continue-on-error: false  # flip once the drift subset is green
    # interim alternative: cargo test -p <green-crates> as a hard job,
    # leaving only known-drift crates in the advisory job

findings.fix_guide: 1) Run cargo test --workspace and bucket failures per crate. 2) Fix or xfail-ignore the framework drift bucket. 3) Flip test-framework's flag first (ubuntu only), observe one week, then flip test-core's ubuntu leg; keep macos/windows advisory if flaky. 4) Update CONTRIBUTING.md 'Advisory jobs' table.

effort_estimate.human_readable: 1-2 days depending on size of the drift bucket
effort_estimate.breakdown: Failure inventory: 60; drift fixes: 360-840; CI flip + observation: 120

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path .github/workflows/ci.yml -Pattern 'continue-on-error' | Select-Object LineNumber, Line; Select-String -Path CONTRIBUTING.md -Pattern 'Advisory jobs'

confidence.rationale: Directly read from ci.yml lines 117/145 and the CONTRIBUTING.md advisory-jobs table; no inference involved.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Verbatim configuration values; also cross-checked against the CONTRIBUTING.md hard-gate table which explicitly separates advisory from gating jobs.

findings.title: Aggregate: 9 of 73 crates have no tests/ directory; buff-lang-ffi-guide has zero tests entirely; 23 crates carry no inline unit tests
findings.description: Census via Glob+Grep (73 crates): (a) 9 crates lack a tests/ dir and rely solely on inline #[cfg(test)]: buff-lang-ast-rsx (1 inline file), buff-lang-buffhtml-parser (3), buff-lang-check (2 files, 45 inline #[test] fns), buff-lang-ffi-guide (0 tests - docs-only crate, lib.rs is 19 lines), buff-lang-fmt (1), buff-lang-pipeline (12 inline matches across 5 src files incl. rustc_invoke.rs and error_mapper.rs), buff-mcp (3), buff-msgpack (1), buff-protobuf (1). (b) 23 crates (mostly framework waves) have a tests/ dir but no inline unit tests. (c) All 44 framework crates have at least one tests/*.rs file (verified per-crate counts; min=1). (d) Snapshot corpus: 285 .snap files across crates. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, integration tests belong in tests/ and inline modules are 'fine for unit smoke' - so (a) is a convention-drift signal, not a violation, EXCEPT buff-lang-pipeline and buff-lang-check, whose lib APIs (compile_rust_to_exe helpers, check_source) are critical-path and only smoke-tested inline; they are exercised indirectly via buff-lang-cli's 40 test files, which is the mitigating golden fallback that keeps this finding at medium rather than high.
findings.root_cause: Crates extracted during ITER module splits (check, fmt, pipeline, mcp, msgpack, protobuf, ast-rsx, buffhtml-parser) inherited coverage through their consumers (mostly buff-lang-cli tests) instead of getting their own tests/ directories.
findings.impact: Consumer-only coverage couples these crates' test signal to another crate's suite: `cargo test -p buff-lang-check` runs 45 inline tests but nothing integration-shaped; a break in buff-lang-pipeline's rustc invocation helpers surfaces only inside buff-lang-cli's suite, obscuring attribution and skipping crate-scoped local-ci runs.
findings.recommendation: Promote the highest-value inline suites to tests/ dirs for the 3 critical-path crates (check, pipeline, buffhtml-parser), and add a 5-line placeholder integration test to the remaining 6 so `cargo test -p <crate>` is never a no-op. Leave docs-only buff-lang-ffi-guide exempt (document the exemption in its AGENTS.md).

fix_examples.before:
// crates/buff-lang-check: no tests/ dir; 45 #[test] fns live in
// src/lib.rs + src/naming_lint.rs inline modules

findings.fix_guide: 1) For check/pipeline/buffhtml-parser: move (not copy) the larger inline suites into tests/*.rs, keeping 2-3 smoke tests inline. 2) For the other 6: add one lib-driving integration test each. 3) Add an exemption note for buff-lang-ffi-guide in its AGENTS.md. 4) Verify with `cargo test -p <crate>` per crate.

effort_estimate.breakdown: check migration: 120; pipeline migration: 120; buffhtml-parser migration: 60; placeholders: 40; verification: 20

detection_method.query: Get-ChildItem crates -Directory | Where { -not (Test-Path "$_/tests") } -> 9; Select-String '#\\[cfg\\(test\\)\\]' crates/*/src -> per-crate match counts

findings.verification_command: Get-ChildItem crates -Directory | Where-Object { -not (Test-Path "$($_.FullName)\tests") } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name; Get-ChildItem crates -Directory | ForEach-Object { $c=(Get-ChildItem "$($_.FullName)\src" -Recurse -Filter *.rs | Select-String '#\[cfg\(test\)\]' -List | Measure-Object).Count; if ($c -eq 0 -and (Test-Path "$($_.FullName)\tests")) { "$($_.Name): tests-dir-only" } }

confidence.rationale: Pure directory/enumeration census, double-run (Test-Path sweep and per-crate Select-String sweep) with agreeing results. ffi-guide verified by full file listing (no test file anywhere in the crate).

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Every 'absence' claim was verified with a directory listing before inclusion; ffi-guide's tests/ absence was confirmed by recursive file enumeration, not just Test-Path. Convention-compliance framing (inline-smoke is permitted) avoids overstating severity.

findings.title: Tautological assertion: test asserts Ok(()) is_ok() with no behavioral content
findings.description: translation.rs line 313-316 (`dap_result_alias_compiles`) constructs `let ok: DapResult<()> = Ok(());` and asserts `ok.is_ok()`. The value is a literal Ok, so the assertion can never fail - the test only proves the type alias exists (which the compiler already proves by compiling). The same file's other tests are strong (message-content asserts, ordering asserts), making this an isolated weak spot. A workspace-wide tautology scan (assert!(true), assert_eq!(true,true), literal-Ok is_ok) found only this instance in crates/*/tests/ (one more inline instance exists at buff-eval/src/lib.rs:841, not context-verified).
findings.root_cause: Type-alias smoke tests written during the T60 DAP proxy spike were kept as placeholder coverage instead of being replaced with behavioral equivalents.
findings.impact: Minimal direct risk, but it inflates the pass count and can mask the absence of real coverage for the DapResult error-conversion path (the interesting behavior - From<DapError>/mapping to protocol errors - is what should be asserted).
findings.recommendation: Replace with a behavioral test of the alias's actual contract: construct a DapError, convert it through the alias's error path, and assert the rendered output; or delete the test if the alias is trivially transparent.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Open crates/buff-dap/src to find DapResult's From/Display impls. 2) Rewrite the test to push a DapError through the alias and assert on rendering. 3) `cargo test -p buff-dap --test translation`.

detection_method.query: regex 'assert!\\(true\\)|assert_eq!\\(true, true\\)|assert!\\(ok\\.is_ok\\(\\)\\)' across crates/**/*.rs -> 2 hits (translation.rs:315, buff-eval src/lib.rs:841)

findings.verification_command: Get-ChildItem crates -Recurse -Filter *.rs | Select-String -Pattern 'assert!\(ok\.is_ok\(\)\)|assert!\(true\)' | Select-Object Path, LineNumber, Line

confidence.rationale: The test body is four lines and fully read; the constructed value is syntactically Ok(()), so the assertion is unconditionally true. No ambiguity.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Direct read of the full test function; zero possibility of hidden setup (no fixtures, no global state).

files_skipped.reason: Static presence census only (Glob/Select-String); full production-source reading out of scope for a coverage audit
Snapshot content not individually reviewed for over-broad redaction; presence counted only
E14xx runtime-code assertions presumed here per crate responsibility; deep audit deferred (flagged as false negative)
Non-Rust or generated-artifact trees outside crate test-coverage scope

falseNegativesIdentified.reason: No cargo test run was performed (static analysis only); currently-failing or ignored tests, flaky tests, and doctest failures are invisible to this audit. Budget for cargo test --workspace exceeded audit scope; CI runs it only as advisory so no authoritative green/red record exists.

Unit-smoke tests embedded in src across ~50 crates were scanned only mechanically; buff-eval/src/lib.rs:841 assert!(ok.is_ok()) was spotted but its surrounding context was not verified, so possible additional tautological/weak inline assertions remain unreported.
cargo test --doc surface (fenced code examples in crate docs, including the ffi-guide GUIDE.md examples) was not audited at all; broken or missing doctests are a blind spot.

285 insta snapshots counted but not diffed against intentional-output; a snapshot that redacts too much (e.g., normalizing away spans) would mask regressions while passing - undetectable without per-snapshot review.
crates/buff-lang-parser/tests/proptest_properties.rs exists but the number/strength of properties and generators coverage vs the grammar surface was not evaluated.
